info.title: DigitalDon Analysis API
info.summary: Machine-readable crypto token analysis — the engine behind @DigitalDonAnalyzeBot and analyzer.digitaldon.net.
info.description:
Structured technical + on-chain analysis for a crypto token.

This is the same analysis engine behind the DigitalDon Telegram bot (`/don`) and
the Web Analyzer, exposed as JSON. All three run one implementation, so the same
token at the same moment scores the same on every surface.

**Depth** controls what is fetched. `basic` is chart + on-chain and costs two
OHLCV requests. `holders` adds a wallet-cluster scan, `social` adds an X
credibility check on the token's linked account, `full` adds both -- each is
slower and rate-limited harder, so ask for what you will read. The `depth` enum
below is this deployment's live menu -- a depth whose feature is switched off is
not listed and cannot be bought -- so read the enum, not this prose.

**Asset class is stated, never implied.** `data.token.asset_class` is `crypto` or
`stock`, matched against a verified issuer registry rather than guessed from the
chain. It matters most on Robinhood Chain, an Arbitrum Orbit L2 for tokenized
equities: a token there is usually a share, not a meme. For one,
`data.token.underlying` carries the ticker, the issuer, and whether the
underlying market is open right now. Holder depths are not sold for tokenized
stocks -- their supply sits in custody wallets, which clustering would report as
insiders.

**Partial results are normal.** A block that could not be produced comes back
`null` with an entry in `data.warnings` explaining why, and the rest of the
response is still valid. Only a request that could produce nothing at all fails.

**No analysis is not an error.** A token too new to have candles returns 200
with `data.analysis.available = false`, `state` telling you whether it is a
fresh launch or a dormant pool, and a populated `data.onchain` block -- which is
the useful read at that point anyway.

**This endpoint is paid, per call, in USDC over
[x402](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402).** Call it without payment and
you get a 402 carrying the price and the accepted chains; sign and retry with a
`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Payment is verified before the analysis runs and
settled only after it succeeds, so a failed scan costs you nothing.

**You only pay for a complete answer.** If any block the depth promised comes
back empty, the request is refused with `depth_undeliverable` and no funds move.

A small number of free calls per day per IP is available at the cheapest depth,
so you can see the output shape before wiring up a wallet. See `x-402` below for
the live price list.

Numbers are advisory, not financial advice.

chain.description: `auto` searches every active chain and analyses the deepest pool, reporting the rest in `data.request.alternatives`. Active on this deployment: arbitrum, arc, base, bsc, ethereum, mantle, robinhood, solana.

depth.description: `basic` = chart + on-chain. `holders` adds wallet clustering, `social` adds an X credibility check, `full` adds both. Only depths this deployment can currently deliver are listed here, and only those can be bought. Holder depths are sold only on solana, where the clustering has a funder graph behind it; asked for elsewhere they are refused with `depth_unavailable` (named chain) or `depth_undeliverable` (chain=auto) and nothing is charged either way.

include_chart_raw.description: Return the OHLCV the analysis ran on. Large.

include_raw_metrics.description: Return every engine field, unshaped and uncontracted.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation. Present on every failure.

schema_version.description: Shape of this document. Parse against it.

engine_version.description: Analysis-logic contract that produced the numbers. Cache against it.

alternatives.description: Other chains this query matched. The deepest pool was analysed; re-request with an explicit `chain` for another.

asset_class.description: What this token IS. `stock` means a tokenized claim on a listed security, matched against a verified issuer registry -- NOT inferred from the chain. Branch on it before applying memecoin priors: Robinhood Chain is an Arbitrum Orbit L2 for tokenized equities, so a token there is usually a share, not a meme. Holder depths are not sold for `stock` -- see `depth`.

underlying.description: The security a tokenized stock is a claim on -- non-null exactly when `asset_class` is `stock`. Read from the curated issuer registry, which is the authority on what is official: a ticker search alone returns copycats. Such a token is also scored on the `STOCK` profile, so `analysis.profile.key` moves with this field.

issuer.description: Who issued the token -- e.g. Robinhood, xStocks.

dual_listed.description: The same underlying is listed by more than one issuer; the other route is in `request.alternatives`.

market_status.description: The UNDERLYING equity market, not the token's pool. The token trades around the clock; its reference price does not.

key.description: Profile the engine scored against — an age band (FRESH / EARLY / ESTABLISHED) or STOCK for a tokenized equity, which is chosen by what the token is rather than by its age. Branch on this.

buy_ratio.description: `null` on a token with no trades -- an empty book is not a balanced one.

analysis.description: Technical analysis. Check `available` before reading the rest.

state.description: `fresh_launch` = too new for candles. `dormant` = old enough, but has barely traded since launch. Do not describe a dormant token as new.

data_quality.description: Candle count, and whether the series was short.

launch_spike_ath.description: True when the high in the history is a launch wick; long-term targets were measured without it.

native.description: Non-null only for DigitalDon's own token, which carries a declared house policy: the score is lifted by `score_lift` and floored at `score_floor`, and the short-term plan is withheld. Null for every other token.

signals.description: Four verdicts, each carrying the raw inputs behind it.

raw.description: Only when options.include_raw_metrics. NOT part of the schema contract -- keys track the engine's internals and may change without a schema major. Prototype against it; ship against the structured blocks.

400.description:
- `depth_unavailable` — `depth` is valid but not sellable on this deployment right now (the feature behind it is switched off). The `detail` names what is.
- `depth_undeliverable` — This token could not be served at the depth paid for, so you were NOT charged. Retry at a depth that fits it; `basic` always works.
- `feature_disabled` — The endpoint is switched off on this deployment.
- `inactive_chain` — `chain` is known but switched off on this deployment.
- `internal` — An upstream call failed. Transient; retry.
- `invalid_depth` — `depth` was not one of the documented values.
- `invalid_request` — Malformed body, or a missing/oversized `token`.
- `no_chart_data` — The token resolved but the OHLCV source returned nothing. Transient; retry.
- `payment_failed` — Settlement failed after the analysis ran, so the result is withheld. No funds moved. Retry.
- `payment_required` — No or invalid payment. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and the `accepts` body field carry what to pay; retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
- `payment_unavailable` — The payment layer is unreachable. The endpoint fails closed rather than serving unpaid. Transient; retry.
- `rate_limited` — Per-IP rate limit exceeded.
- `token_not_found` — No pool matched the query (on the requested chain, if one was given).
- `unknown_chain` — `chain` is not a chain this API knows.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation. Present on every failure.

- `depth_undeliverable` — This token could not be served at the depth paid for, so you were NOT charged. Retry at a depth that fits it; `basic` always works.
- `feature_disabled` — The endpoint is switched off on this deployment.
- `inactive_chain` — `chain` is known but switched off on this deployment.
- `internal` — An upstream call failed. Transient; retry.
- `invalid_depth` — `depth` was not one of the documented values.
- `invalid_request` — Malformed body, or a missing/oversized `token`.
- `no_chart_data` — The token resolved but the OHLCV source returned nothing. Transient; retry.
- `payment_failed` — Settlement failed after the analysis ran, so the result is withheld. No funds moved. Retry.
- `payment_required` — No or invalid payment. The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and the `accepts` body field carry what to pay; retry with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
- `payment_unavailable` — The payment layer is unreachable. The endpoint fails closed rather than serving unpaid. Transient; retry.
- `rate_limited` — Per-IP rate limit exceeded.
- `token_not_found` — No pool matched the query (on the requested chain, if one was given).
- `unknown_chain` — `chain` is not a chain this API knows.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation. Present on every failure.

get.summary: This document. The address x402 directories look at.
This document, at its versioned address.

x-cache.note: Repeat calls for the same token inside `analysis_seconds` are served from one memoised scan, so the numbers are identical -- `generated_at` is when the DOCUMENT was built, not when the data was read. A cache hit is still charged: the price is for the answer, not for our upstream request. The cache is in-memory and per-process, so treat these as freshness bounds, not guarantees. Key your own cache on `engine_version`.

x-rate-limit.note: Exceeding it returns 429 with error `rate_limited`. Depth beyond `basic` is additionally bounded by a server-side concurrency cap, so a burst of deep scans queues rather than failing.
